newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU governments-Parliament at odds on book pricing.
newsitem.headline: EU governments-Parliament at odds on book pricing.

text.p: EU culture ministers and the European Commission were at odds on Tuesday over whether cross-border agreements on book pricing should be allowed to continue.

At the two-day informal meeting of EU culture ministers the EU's Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said he opposed the type of accord operated by same-language areas like Germany, Austria and Switzerland on the grounds that they amount to an anti-competitive cartel under EU competition law.

But Dutch State Secretary for Education, Culture and Science Aad Nuis said ministers had backed such price fixing schemes and believed books were a matter of culture and thus governed by the principle of subsidiarity.

"We saw that we have diametrically opposed opinions," he told a news conference, saying the Commission had now been charged with finding a legally acceptable solution to allow the systems to fit in with EU competition policy and put an end to its reservations.
"What you have to do is closely scrutinise the arguments on each side," he said.

A large number of member states have systems of fixed book prices -- whether laid down in law or agreed by sector self-regulation -- and the Commission and Council have been grappling for some time over how to make cross-border language accords fit in with the EU's rules.
